result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by narrow sidewalks and a wide roadway containing embedded trolley tracks, which present a tripping hazard. There is a complete lack of marked crossings or traffic calming measures, and sightlines are significantly obscured by continuous on-street parking.

hazards.name: Trolley Tracks
hazards.description: Embedded tracks in the roadway create a trip hazard for pedestrians and a slip/entrapment hazard for cyclists.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking blocks sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers in the roadway.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: No designated or protected crossing points are visible, forcing pedestrians to cross the wide roadway unprotected.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) at potential crossing points to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Mark mid-block or intersection crossings with high-visibility paint to alert drivers to pedestrian presence.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Add lighting specifically directed at the sidewalk and crossing areas to improve nighttime safety and visibility.

result.summary: The image shows a narrow residential street lined with row houses. Pedestrians have a very constrained walkway that is further obstructed by utility poles and closely parked vehicles.

hazards.name: Narrow Sidewalk
hazards.description: The sidewalk is extremely narrow, making it difficult for two people to pass or for someone with a mobility device to navigate.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the right side of the street in front of the houses.

hazards.name: Utility Pole Obstruction
hazards.description: A large wooden utility pole is placed directly in the middle of the narrow sidewalk, further restricting pedestrian movement.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening
interventions.description: Expand the sidewalk width by reallocating space from the roadway or parking lane to meet ADA standards.

interventions.title: Utility Undergrounding or Relocation
interventions.description: Move utility poles to the furniture zone or underground to clear the pedestrian through-zone.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffer Zone
interventions.description: Install street trees or a planting strip to provide a physical and psychological buffer between pedestrians and parked/moving vehicles.

result.summary: The image shows a residential street with row houses and integrated streetcar tracks. While sidewalks are present on both sides, the environment lacks marked pedestrian crossings and features significant visual obstructions from parked vehicles.

hazards.name: Streetcar tracks
hazards.description: The embedded tracks create uneven surfaces and potential tripping hazards for pedestrians crossing the street.

hazards.name: Visual obstructions
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the street limits sightlines between drivers and pedestrians attempting to cross.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at intersections to shorten crossing distances and move pedestrians into the driver's line of sight beyond parked cars.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add high-visibility marked crosswalks to designate safe crossing points and alert drivers to pedestrian presence.

interventions.title: Street Trees
interventions.description: Plant street trees to provide a vertical element that naturally slows traffic and improves the pedestrian experience.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment consists of a narrow sidewalk on a residential street where private stoops significantly reduce the clear walking path. Parked cars line the curb, creating a visual barrier between pedestrians and the single travel lane, while the lack of traffic calming or street trees limits the overall safety and comfort of the streetscape.

hazards.name: Narrow effective sidewalk
hazards.description: Residential stoops and stairs extend into the public right-of-way, reducing the clear walking width to less than 4 feet in many places.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the sidewalk where house stoops meet the walkway.

hazards.name: Visual screening
hazards.description: A continuous line of parked vehicles obscures sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers in the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: The row of parked vehicles along the curb line.

interventions.title: Speed Humps
interventions.description: Install asphalt speed humps to physically limit vehicle speeds in this residential context.

interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at the nearest intersections to improve visibility and reduce the distance pedestrians must spend in the roadway.

interventions.title: Street Trees
interventions.description: Introduce street trees in the parking lane or sidewalk buffer to provide shade and a psychological narrowing of the street to slow traffic.
